concepts.label: Prometheus discovery API endpoint (/prometheus_sd_config)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - genuinely new territory, as the round's hypothesis anticipated: Couchbase Server's own Prometheus-integration vocabulary (a service-discovery endpoint returning the cluster's node list in Prometheus's own config format) has no analogue in the Capella-specific monitoring: family and doesn't fit it.

concepts.label: File-based Prometheus service discovery

concepts.label: HTTP Prometheus service discovery
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the sibling configuration method (Prometheus calls the discovery API endpoint directly and periodically, via http_sd_configs).

relations.subject: prometheus:legacy-discovery-endpoint
relations.evidence: Prior to version 7.2.1, an endpoint named `/prometheus_sd_config.yaml` was the best way to configure Prometheus to collect metrics from Couchbase Server. This endpoint is now deprecated because the new `/prometheus_sd_config` discovery API endpoint offers more features.

relations.subject: role:external-stats-reader
relations.evidence: Assign this user the External Stats Reader role which grants it the ability to call the discovery API. This role also gives it the ability to read Couchbase Server's metrics.

relations.subject: cert:root-certificate
relations.evidence: Save the file to a location in your Prometheus host. When you configure your Prometheus job to collect metrics from Couchbase Server, add the file to the job definition's `tls_config` section.

relations.subject: prometheus:file-based-service-discovery
relations.evidence: With this method, you have to take additional steps to update the list if you change the nodes in your Couchbase Database.

relations.subject: prometheus:http-service-discovery
relations.evidence: This method has the benefit that Prometheus defaults to periodically calling the endpoint so it automatically learns of any added or removed nodes.

relations.subject: prometheus:app-telemetry
relations.evidence: Couchbase Server reports the collected data as metrics through the same Prometheus endpoint that it uses to report its own metrics.

relations.subject: prometheus:app-telemetry
relations.evidence: Application telemetry is disabled by default in Couchbase Server 8.0

relations.subject: prometheus:app-telemetry
relations.evidence: See [Application Telemetry](../../rest-api/application-telemetry.md) to learn how to enable application telemetry.

notable_absence.finding: 'We strongly recommend against reading /proc/[pid]/smaps for processes with large RSS; for example, Couchbase Server's Data and Index Services (memcached and indexer)... we have seen delays of 10-20 seconds.' This is a direct, named warning against a common Prometheus exporter behavior (process_exporter's gather-smaps option, also embedded in Grafana Alloy/Agent) that can itself degrade the cluster it's meant to monitor - a monitoring-tool-induced performance hazard with no equivalent warning anywhere else in this batch, including the troubleshoot/ pages, which document performance degradation from split-lock mitigation and swappiness but not from monitoring tooling itself.

cross_component_finding: This page confirms the round's hypothesis directly: Server's own Prometheus/metrics vocabulary (discovery API, file-based vs HTTP service discovery, per-node Prometheus instance, application telemetry) shares nothing structurally with the Capella-specific monitoring: family (event severity enums, health-advisor reports, activity log) - it is genuinely new territory, minted here under a new prometheus: namespace rather than forced into monitoring:. Separately, prometheus:app-telemetry is the first place in this batch where Couchbase SDK client applications (not just the server cluster) become monitorable subjects through a Server-side Prometheus surface, a cross-product data path from the SDKs into Server's own metrics endpoint.
cross_product_finding: Application Telemetry aggregates metrics from SDK client applications ('applications that use the Couchbase SDKs') across all clients into the same Prometheus surface Couchbase Server uses for its own metrics - the first SDK-to-Server-monitoring data path found in this batch, letting an operator 'monitor the health of both your Couchbase Server cluster and your applications that use the Couchbase SDKs' from one Prometheus target.
